recommendation: Keep the empty audit commit as-is. No FHIR core follow-up is needed unless a future work-group decision adds a distinct status reason extension or additional final statuses.
issue_request: FHIR-12315 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core QuestionnaireAnswers change request asking for a QuestionnaireResponse status representing a response that was not completed and was not expected to be revisited. The accepted PC resolution was to add `stopped` rather than encode inability-to-complete as a separate status reason.
initial_application: The issue was applied in git-svn commit f3f2ad2c4b57ba4d2dfbbd990363885b40b49101 on 2017-01-06, which added `stopped` to the old QuestionnaireResponse spreadsheet source and added committee note GF#12315 to QuestionnaireResponse.status. The 2021 source rework preserved the status in the current XML CodeSystem and StructureDefinition source.
additional_context: QuestionnaireResponse is an active build resource in source/fhir.ini. The current StructureDefinition includes `stopped` in QuestionnaireResponse.status and binds the element to ValueSet/questionnaire-answers-status; the current CodeSystem defines `stopped`. Later Published issue FHIR-20767 intentionally clarified `stopped` as the terminal incomplete/abandoned state and declined separate `incomplete` or `expired` codes. Zulip and Confluence searches found no conflicting work-group record; a later implementer thread aligned with the interpretation that `stopped` means choosing not to finish and does not encode why.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current active source already carries the requested code, and the difference between FHIR-12315's original definition text and the current definition is explained by the later FHIR-20767 clarification.

related_jiras.note: Later Published decision clarified `stopped` as terminal incomplete/abandoned and explains why the current definition differs from FHIR-12315's original wording.
